phase.validation: passed: format/build/test/docs/complexity; see validation.json and toolchain-result.json
phase.note: Individual finding statuses below record triage dispositions; this phase record tracks subsequent editing/review/validation. Deferred parts remain open.

evidence_depth: source-read, test-read, spec-compared; no execution or hardware verification during investigation

findings.claim: Secret ownership, initialization-only assignment, and disposal scope are underspecified; parsed output says exclusively owns its secret.
findings.evidence: Direct initialization retains the supplied array; Secret exposes it; Dispose clears that same array. ParseUri allocates decoded storage but cannot clear input URI/immutable encoded strings.
findings.disposition: Accept factual initialization/aliasing/disposal clarification now; do not promise PUT preservation, consumption or reuse pending F02.
findings.confidence: high for source facts; PUT ownership intent unresolved

findings.claim: PUT has no consuming contract but clears the original Secret for some key lengths.
findings.evidence: HmacShortenKey and PadSecret both return the input for lengths 14..hash-block-size; PUT clears that returned array in finally. Other lengths use new arrays. Existing payload tests do not establish preservation/reuse.
findings.disposition: Establish consistent ownership and retry/disposal semantics; test boundaries and failed sends. Do not document length-dependent mutation as intentional.

findings.claim: Decoded secret arrays are not explicitly cleared when parsing later fails.
findings.evidence: Algorithm/integer/period checks can throw after secret decoding. Base32 validation can throw after partially writing the output array. No object is returned for caller disposal.
findings.disposition: Fix failure-path ownership/cleanup with meaningful regression evidence; do not promise comprehensive parser cleanup meanwhile.

findings.claim: URI is described as defined by Google Authenticator Key URI Format despite acceptance differences.
findings.evidence: HOTP counter defaults to zero although required by format; query issuer wins despite differing label issuer; extra colons and arbitrary int digits accepted. Issuer equality is SHOULD guidance, unlike required counter.
findings.disposition: Decide strictness/extensions before changing conformance wording or validation. Existing tests encode some permissive behavior but do not prove deliberate v2 policy.

findings.claim: Base32 decoding silently accepts impossible terminal encoding lengths.
findings.evidence: Output length is floor(length*5/8); terminal quantum is not validated. Input A yields no output byte; subsequent padding can yield an all-zero processed key. RFC 4648 section 6 describes valid terminal forms.
findings.disposition: Validate encoding shape in both paths and use exact-byte/malformed vectors. Pad-bit rejection is a separate RFC 4648 section 3.5 policy question.
findings.confidence: high for source path; no runtime reproduction

findings.claim: Creation accepts identifiers that decode with different metadata or are later omitted.
findings.evidence: Unqualified TOTP name 60/demo with period 30 formats as 60/demo but parses with period 60. Colons change issuer parsing; direct period zero produces a prefix that response parsing rejects; empty issuer behavior differs.
findings.disposition: Define valid component syntax and creation-boundary checks, preserving raw IDs separately from host convention. Do not assume device acceptance was tested.
findings.confidence: high for host transformations; device acceptance unverified

findings.claim: Negative period prefixes reportedly throw, and guidance gives a Unicode-digit regex.
findings.evidence: Actual pattern uses [0-9]+; -30/demo is an ordinary name, not a recognized prefix. Recognized zero/overflow prefixes throw.
findings.disposition: Document ASCII-decimal recognized prefixes and positive int range; distinguish the host ID convention from YKOATH grammar. Prefer source reference over duplicating the full regex if clearer.

findings.claim: Creation docs omit firmware minimums for SHA-512 and touch while implying only two features need newer firmware.
findings.evidence: Official YKOATH ALGORITHMS requires SHA-512 firmware 4.3.1; PROPERTIES requires touch 4.2.4. PUT contains no SDK preflight guard for either.
findings.disposition: Add device requirements, distinguishing them from SDK-gated rename/SCP03. Do not promise NotSupportedException or add guards/session floors.
findings.confidence: high, primary protocol corroborated by coordinator

findings.claim: Fourteen-byte storage padding is called minimum HMAC key size.
findings.evidence: RFC 2104 sections 2-3 defines no 14-byte HMAC minimum. Source pads to 14; YKOATH PUT page gives no rationale. Another SDK's matching constant is only corroboration.
findings.disposition: Describe the SDK storage-padding threshold, preserving behavior. Do not claim entropy increase or a device requirement; defer historical rationale/constant naming decision.

findings.claim: PUT is described only as storing a new credential.
findings.evidence: Official YKOATH PUT says adds or overwrites; SDK sends PUT without an existence check.
findings.disposition: Document replacement by existing raw credential ID in API/README; no runtime existence check or CLI prompt behavior change in this batch.
findings.confidence: high for protocol/source; no hardware claim

findings.claim: Requested numeric creation values can be silently changed during wire encoding.
findings.evidence: Digits int narrows to byte without validation; no checked-overflow setting found in project configuration. Negative HOTP counters omit IMF because emission requires >0. Protocol specifies four-byte IMF without resolving all supported ranges here.
findings.disposition: Define and validate supported digit/counter ranges with boundary tests. Distinguish device-supported digits from Google URI 6/8 syntax. Do not bless silent narrowing or negative-to-default behavior.
findings.confidence: high for encoding path, device ranges unresolved

findings.evidence: Both remove literal ASCII spaces only; tabs/newlines remain invalid alphabet characters.
findings.disposition: Say spaces rather than whitespace. Do not change decoder validation or make a broad conformance claim; F05 remains open.

findings.claim: Table lists TOTP/HOTP followed by 0x10/0x20, implying reversed association.
findings.evidence: Enum and official YKOATH TYPES map HOTP=0x10 and TOTP=0x20.
findings.disposition: Make the association explicit in the table; verify other table entries against constants.

findings.claim: requireTouch true makes every calculation wait for touch.
findings.evidence: Bulk CALCULATE ALL returns null for touch-required entries and does not wait; source and YKOATH agree.
findings.disposition: Describe touch for individual calculations, preserving the bulk exception or pointing to the adjacent calculate section.
